facts.condition: Necessary screening rule: if a finite blocklength-two auxiliary construction has a Marton objective above the doubled optimal one-symbol randomized-time-division baseline, then its binary-input covariance κ obeys κ² < 7 ln(2)/248, and therefore |κ| < 0.14.

assumptions: κ is the covariance of the two binary channel inputs under the candidate's induced two-use input law.
The Marton objective and randomized-time-division baseline use the canonical problem's established normalization.
The rule applies only to finite blocklength-two candidates and does not itself establish achievability, exclusion of all gains, tensorization, or a capacity converse.
